records.source: אָמַ֤רְתִּֽי אֲנִי֙ בְּלִבִּ֔י לְכָה־נָּ֛א אֲנַסְּכָ֛ה בְשִׂמְחָ֖ה וּרְאֵ֣ה בְט֑וֹב וְהִנֵּ֥ה גַם־ה֖וּא הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: I said, I, in my heart: Come now, let me test you with pleasure, and look on good; and look, also it [was] breath.
pieces: I said to myself, "Come, let me try you out with pleasure; enjoy what is good." But this too was a breath.

L.1: I said in my heart, "Come now, let me test you with joy; so look on what is good." And look, this too [was] breath.

R.1: I said to myself, "Come on, I will try out pleasure. Enjoy yourself!" But this too was like a breath.

decisions.choice: let me test you: Qoheleth speaks to his own heart
decisions.reason: He addresses his heart, that is, himself, as in 1:16. He sets out to test pleasure as he tested wisdom, keeping his wisdom as his guide (verse 3).

decisions.choice: pleasure: joy, enjoyment
decisions.reason: The word (simchah) is joy or gladness. In this chapter it is the pleasure a king can buy (verses 4-10). Later in the book the same joy is a gift of God to be received (2:26; 5:19; 8:15).

decisions.choice: look on what is good: enjoy good things
decisions.reason: "To see good" is a Hebrew way of saying to enjoy or experience it (3:13; 5:17; Psalm 34:13).

decisions.choice: breath: it left nothing lasting
decisions.reason: Pleasure did not satisfy or remain; here hevel leans toward "empty", what has no lasting result (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: I said to myself
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the English idiom (see 1:16). The words he says to himself take double quotation marks.

decisions.choice: like a breath
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the breath picture with "like", as the founder ruled for hevel outside 1:2 and 12:8.

records.heading: Testing pleasure and great works

records.source: לִשְׂח֖וֹק אָמַ֣רְתִּי מְהוֹלָ֑ל וּלְשִׂמְחָ֖ה מַה־זֹּ֥ה עֹשָֽׂה׃
records.gloss: Of laughter I said: Mad! and of pleasure: What [is] this doing?
pieces: I said of laughter, "It is madness," and of pleasure, "What good does it do?"

L.2: Of laughter I said, "[It is] mad," and of joy, "What does this accomplish?"

R.2: I said, "Laughter is foolish. And what good does pleasure do?"

decisions.choice: mad: senseless
decisions.reason: The word (mehollal) is a passive form of the verb behind "madness" in 1:17: laughter makes people act without sense.

decisions.choice: what does this accomplish: a question expecting the answer "nothing"
decisions.reason: Pleasure produces nothing that remains, which is the point of "gain" (1:3).

decisions.choice: foolish
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plain word for the sense (m1).

records.source: תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י לִמְשׁ֥וֹךְ בַּיַּ֖יִן אֶת־בְּשָׂרִ֑י וְלִבִּ֞י נֹהֵ֤ג בַּֽחָכְמָה֙ וְלֶאֱחֹ֣ז בְּסִכְל֔וּת עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁר־אֶרְאֶ֗ה אֵי־זֶ֨ה ט֜וֹב לִבְנֵ֤י הָאָדָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר יַעֲשׂוּ֙ תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם מִסְפַּ֖ר יְמֵ֥י חַיֵּיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: I searched in my heart to draw my flesh with wine, and my heart guiding with wisdom, and to take hold of folly, until I might see where this [is] good for the sons of humankind which they do under the heavens [for] the number of the days of their lives.
pieces: I explored with my mind how to cheer my body with wine, while my mind still guided me with wisdom, and how to take up folly, until I could see what is good for human beings to do under the heavens during the few days of their lives.

L.3: I explored in my heart how to draw my body along with wine, while my heart [was] guiding [me] with wisdom, and how to take hold of folly, until I might see what [is] good for the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}} to do under the heavens [for] the number of the days of their life.

R.3: I decided to find out what it is like to enjoy wine, while still letting wisdom guide me. I wanted to try foolish things too. I wanted to see what is good for people to do in this world during the short time they live.

decisions.choice: draw my body with wine: refresh or cheer it with wine
decisions.reason: The verb (mashakh) means to draw or drag. With wine it most likely means to cheer or refresh the body, to be carried along by wine's pleasure. The exact picture is not clear.

decisions.choice: my heart guiding with wisdom: he kept his wisdom while he tested pleasure
decisions.reason: The clause stands in the middle of the sentence. He did not give himself up to drunkenness; he tried out pleasure and folly with his wisdom still in charge, as an experiment (2:9).

decisions.choice: explored: searched out, the verb of 1:13
decisions.reason: The verb (tur) is the one used in 1:13 for his search by wisdom.

decisions.choice: the number of the days of their life: the short, counted days of life
decisions.reason: Days that can be numbered are few (5:17; 6:12; Psalm 90:12).

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings, men and women; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

decisions.choice: the few days of their lives (B); the short time they live (R)
alternatives: the number of the days of their life
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the counting of days implies (m4).

records.source: הִגְדַּ֖לְתִּי מַעֲשָׂ֑י בָּנִ֤יתִי לִי֙ בָּתִּ֔ים נָטַ֥עְתִּי לִ֖י כְּרָמִֽים׃
records.gloss: I made great my works: I built for myself houses, I planted for myself vineyards.
pieces: I undertook great works. I built houses for myself and planted vineyards for myself.

L.4: I made my works great: I built houses for myself; I planted vineyards for myself.

R.4: I did great things. I built houses and planted vineyards for myself.

decisions.choice: great works: the building of a great king, recalling Solomon
decisions.reason: The list in verses 4-8 recalls what is told of Solomon: his palace and buildings (1 Kings 7:1-12; 9:15-19), his wealth (1 Kings 10:14-27) and a vineyard of his (Song 8:11). See the note at 1:1 on the speaker.

decisions.choice: for myself: all of it for his own pleasure
decisions.reason: "For myself" is repeated through verses 4-8. He tests what a person can gain by building and gathering for himself.

records.source: עָשִׂ֣יתִי לִ֔י גַּנּ֖וֹת וּפַרְדֵּסִ֑ים וְנָטַ֥עְתִּי בָהֶ֖ם עֵ֥ץ כָּל־פֶּֽרִי׃
records.gloss: I made for myself gardens and parks, and I planted in them trees of every fruit.
pieces: I made gardens and parks for myself and planted all kinds of fruit trees in them.

L.5: I made for myself gardens and parks, and I planted in them trees of every [kind of] fruit.

R.5: I made gardens and parks and planted every kind of fruit tree in them.

decisions.choice: parks: walled gardens or orchards
decisions.reason: The word (pardes) is a loanword from Persian for an enclosed park. It is used of the king's forest in Nehemiah 2:8 and of an orchard in Song 4:13. The Greek word paradeisos, "paradise", comes from the same Persian word.

decisions.choice: trees of every fruit: an abundance like a garden of God
decisions.reason: Gardens with every kind of tree recall the garden of Eden, where God made every tree good for food to grow (Genesis 2:9). Qoheleth makes such a garden for himself.

records.source: עָשִׂ֥יתִי לִ֖י בְּרֵכ֣וֹת מָ֑יִם לְהַשְׁק֣וֹת מֵהֶ֔ם יַ֖עַר צוֹמֵ֥חַ עֵצִֽים׃
records.gloss: I made for myself pools of water, to water from them a forest sprouting trees.
pieces: I made myself pools of water to irrigate a forest of growing trees.

L.6: I made for myself pools of water, to water from them a forest sprouting trees.

R.6: I made pools to hold water for watering my forests of young trees.

decisions.choice: pools: large reservoirs for storing water
decisions.reason: Pools cut in rock or built of stone stored water through the dry summer, and kings were remembered for building them (2 Kings 20:20; Nehemiah 2:14; Song 7:5).

decisions.choice: a forest sprouting trees: a plantation of young, growing trees
decisions.reason: The participle "sprouting" shows that the trees were young and growing.

decisions.choice: to hold water
decisions.reason: Readable says what the pools were for.

records.source: קָנִ֨יתִי֙ עֲבָדִ֣ים וּשְׁפָח֔וֹת וּבְנֵי־בַ֖יִת הָ֣יָה לִ֑י גַּ֣ם מִקְנֶה֩ בָקָ֨ר וָצֹ֤אן הַרְבֵּה֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י מִכֹּ֛ל שֶֽׁהָי֥וּ לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: I acquired male slaves and female slaves, and sons of the house were to me; also livestock, herd and flock, much was to me, more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.
pieces: I bought male and female slaves, and I had slaves born in my household. I also owned more herds and flocks than anyone who had been before me in Jerusalem.

L.7: I acquired male slaves and female slaves, and I had slaves born in [my] house; also I had livestock, herds and flocks, much more than all who were before me in Jerusalem.

R.7: I bought men and women as slaves, and I had slaves born in my house. I also owned more cattle, sheep and goats than anyone in Jerusalem before me.

decisions.choice: slaves: people owned, not hired
decisions.reason: The verb (qanah) means to acquire or buy, and is used for buying slaves (Exodus 21:2). These men and women were his property, as were those born to them in his house.

decisions.choice: sons of the house: slaves born in the household
decisions.reason: "A son of my house" is a slave born in the household (Genesis 15:3), who belonged to the master from birth (Genesis 17:12).

decisions.choice: livestock, herds and flocks: cattle, and sheep and goats
decisions.reason: "Herd" (baqar) is cattle; "flock" (tson) is sheep and goats together.

decisions.choice: slaves
decisions.reason: Here slavery itself is the point: people were bought and owned as property (m1), so every level keeps "slave", as the style guide sets for such passages.

decisions.choice: cattle, sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Readable names the animals (m3).

records.source: כָּנַ֤סְתִּי לִי֙ גַּם־כֶּ֣סֶף וְזָהָ֔ב וּסְגֻלַּ֥ת מְלָכִ֖ים וְהַמְּדִינ֑וֹת עָשִׂ֨יתִי לִ֜י שָׁרִ֣ים וְשָׁר֗וֹת וְתַעֲנוּגֹ֛ת בְּנֵ֥י הָאָדָ֖ם שִׁדָּ֥ה וְשִׁדּֽוֹת׃
records.gloss: I gathered for myself also silver and gold, and treasure of kings and the provinces; I made for myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of the sons of humankind, a shiddah and shiddot.
pieces: I amassed silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and provinces. I got myself male and female singers, and what people delight in most: many concubines.

L.8: I gathered for myself both silver and gold, and the treasure of kings and the provinces; I got for myself male singers and female singers, and the delights of the {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}, a concubine and concubines.

R.8: I also collected silver and gold, and the treasures of kings and of lands. I had men and women to sing for me, and I had what people enjoy most, a harem of many women.

decisions.choice: the treasure of kings and provinces: the riches that kings and lands bring as tribute or gifts
decisions.reason: The word (segullah) is a treasured possession, used of Israel as God's own in Exodus 19:5, and here of royal wealth. Kings and provinces paid tribute and brought gifts to a great king (1 Kings 10:14-15, 25). "Provinces" (medinot) is a later word for regions under a ruler (Esther 1:1).

decisions.choice: a concubine and concubines: many women for the king's pleasure
decisions.reason: The pair (shiddah veshiddot) occurs only here, and its meaning is not known for certain. After "the delights of men" most take it to mean a concubine or mistress, and the form, a singular followed by its plural, means "very many". Solomon had many wives and concubines (1 Kings 11:3). Some link the word with the word for "breast", others with a word for a lady. The ancient Greek translation read "a cupbearer and female cupbearers", and other old translations read cups and jars.

decisions.choice: the delights of the sons of men: what people take most pleasure in
decisions.reason: The word (ta'anugot) is delight or luxury; it is used of love's pleasures in Song 7:7 and of comfort in Proverbs 19:10.

decisions.choice: {{gender:children of humankind|sons of men}}
decisions.reason: The phrase means human beings in general; the gender setting gives the inclusive form by default (see 1:13).

decisions.choice: many concubines (B); a harem of many women (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the Hebrew form means, "very many" (m2). Readable uses "harem", a word more readers know than "concubine"; it says the same, no more and no less.

records.source: וְגָדַ֣לְתִּי וְהוֹסַ֔פְתִּי מִכֹּ֛ל שֶׁהָיָ֥ה לְפָנַ֖י בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם אַ֥ף חָכְמָתִ֖י עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי׃
records.gloss: And I became great and I increased more than all who were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom stood by me.
pieces: So I became great, greater than all who were before me in Jerusalem, and my wisdom stayed with me.

L.9: So I became great and surpassed all who were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom stood by me.

R.9: I became greater than anyone who had been in Jerusalem before me. And I still kept my wisdom.

decisions.choice: my wisdom stood by me: it stayed with him and kept serving him
decisions.reason: As he said in verse 3, he tested pleasure with his wisdom in charge. Wisdom did not leave him while he enjoyed his wealth.

decisions.choice: I became great and increased: I grew greater and greater
decisions.reason: The two verbs say one thing: his greatness kept growing (1:16).

records.source: וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָֽׁאֲל֣וּ עֵינַ֔י לֹ֥א אָצַ֖לְתִּי מֵהֶ֑ם לֹֽא־מָנַ֨עְתִּי אֶת־לִבִּ֜י מִכָּל־שִׂמְחָ֗ה כִּֽי־לִבִּ֤י שָׂמֵ֨חַ֙ מִכָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י וְזֶֽה־הָיָ֥ה חֶלְקִ֖י מִכָּל־עֲמָלִֽי׃
records.gloss: And all that my eyes asked I did not withhold from them; I did not restrain my heart from any pleasure, for my heart [was] joyful from all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.
pieces: I did not keep from my eyes anything they desired, and I did not refuse my heart any pleasure. My heart took pleasure in all my hard work, and this was my share for all my hard work.

L.10: And all that my eyes asked for I did not withhold from them; I did not hold back my heart from any joy, for my heart was glad from all my toil, and this was my portion from all my toil.

R.10: I gave myself everything I wanted. I did not stop myself from enjoying anything. I was happy with all my hard work, and that joy was what life gave me for all my hard work.

decisions.choice: portion: the share that falls to a person
decisions.reason: The word (cheleq) is a share of land or of plunder (Genesis 14:24; Joshua 18:7), the part given to someone. In this book it is the share of life a person is given to enjoy now (3:22; 5:17-18; 9:6, 9), not a lasting gain. Qoheleth's joy was the share he had from his work. Whether that share is enough is the question of the next verse.

decisions.choice: all that my eyes asked: everything I desired
decisions.reason: The eyes stand for desire (1:8; 4:8).

decisions.choice: joyful from all my toil: he found joy in his work and in what it produced
alternatives: joy as a result of the toil
decisions.reason: The small word "from" can mean "in" or "because of"; both fit, since he enjoyed both the work and its fruit.

decisions.choice: share (B); what life gave me (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for cheleq: "portion" at Literal, "share" at Balanced, "what life gives you" at Readable, here put in the past to fit the sentence.

decisions.choice: I gave myself everything I wanted
alternatives: all that my eyes asked I did not withhold from them
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the eyes asking means (m2).

records.source: וּפָנִ֣יתִֽי אֲנִ֗י בְּכָל־מַעֲשַׂי֙ שֶֽׁעָשׂ֣וּ יָדַ֔י וּבֶֽעָמָ֖ל שֶׁעָמַ֣לְתִּי לַעֲשׂ֑וֹת וְהִנֵּ֨ה הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֨בֶל֙ וּרְע֣וּת ר֔וּחַ וְאֵ֥ין יִתְר֖וֹן תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I turned, I, to all my works which my hands had done, and to the toil which I had toiled to do; and look, the all [was] breath and a chasing of wind, and there was no gain under the sun.
pieces: Then I looked at all that my hands had done and at the hard work I had spent in doing it, and I found that everything was a breath and chasing the wind. Nothing was gained under the sun.

L.11: Then I turned to all my works that my hands had done, and to the toil at which I had toiled in doing them, and look, everything [was] breath and a chasing of wind, and there [was] no gain under the sun.

R.11: Then I looked at everything I had done and all the hard work it took. All of it was like a breath. It was like trying to catch the wind. None of it did any lasting good here on earth.

decisions.choice: breath: it left nothing lasting
decisions.reason: Here hevel leans toward "empty", what leaves no lasting result, as the end of the verse says (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: no gain: nothing left over, the answer to 1:3
decisions.reason: The question of 1:3, "what gain is there?", has its answer: when everything was added up, nothing remained (see the note on yitron at 1:3).

decisions.choice: I turned: I turned to look at, I considered
decisions.reason: The verb (panah) is to turn, here to turn and look (2:12).

decisions.choice: a breath and chasing the wind ... Nothing was gained (B); like a breath ... like trying to catch the wind ... did any lasting good (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for hevel, re'ut ruach and yitron (see 1:2, 1:3, 1:14). Readable adds "lasting", which is what "gain" means here (m2).

decisions.choice: I found that
decisions.reason: As in 1:14, Balanced says what "look" marks.

records.source: וּפָנִ֤יתִֽי אֲנִי֙ לִרְא֣וֹת חָכְמָ֔ה וְהוֹלֵל֖וֹת וְסִכְל֑וּת כִּ֣י׀מֶ֣ה הָאָדָ֗ם שֶׁיָּבוֹא֙ אַחֲרֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־כְּבָ֖ר עָשֽׂוּהוּ׃
records.gloss: And I turned, I, to see wisdom and madness and folly; for what [is] the man who will come after the king? [That] which already they have done.
pieces: Then I turned to look at wisdom, and at madness and folly. For what can the one who comes after the king do? Only what has already been done.

L.12: And I turned to consider wisdom and madness and folly; for what [can] the man [do] who comes after the king? What [has] already [been] done.

R.12: Then I thought about wisdom, and about madness and foolishness. What can anyone who comes after the king do? Only what has been done before.

decisions.choice: what can the man who comes after the king do? Only what has already been done
alternatives: what is the man who comes after the king? He is what was made long ago
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief and hard: "for what the man who comes after the king, what already they have done". Most take it to mean that a successor, or anyone who tries the king's test again, can only do what has been done before (1:9-10); he will find nothing new. "They have done" may stand for "what has been done". The verse also prepares for verses 18-19, where Qoheleth thinks of the man who will come after him.

decisions.choice: wisdom and madness and folly: as in 1:17
decisions.reason: He comes back to the comparison he set out to make in 1:17, and verses 13-16 give what he found.

decisions.choice: [can] ... [do] ... [has] ... [been]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words English needs to make sense of the short Hebrew (m1).

decisions.choice: anyone
decisions.reason: The words do not name a particular person; Readable says "anyone", which keeps both the successor and anyone else in view.

records.source: וְרָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי שֶׁיֵּ֥שׁ יִתְר֛וֹן לַֽחָכְמָ֖ה מִן־הַסִּכְל֑וּת כִּֽיתְר֥וֹן הָא֖וֹר מִן־הַחֹֽשֶׁךְ׃
records.gloss: And I saw, I, that there is advantage to wisdom more than folly, like the advantage of light more than darkness.
pieces: And I saw that there is more gain in wisdom than in folly, just as there is more gain in light than in darkness.

L.13: And I saw that there is gain for wisdom over folly, as the gain of light over darkness.

R.13: I saw that wisdom does more good than foolishness, just as light does more good than darkness.

decisions.choice: gain: here an advantage of one thing over another
decisions.reason: The word (yitron, see 1:3) means what is left over. Here it measures wisdom against folly: wisdom has the edge, as light has over darkness. Verses 14-16 add that this edge does not outlast death.

decisions.choice: wisdom is better than folly: a real advantage set beside a shared end
decisions.reason: The book does not take back what it says here when it goes on to say that the wise die like fools (verses 14-16). Both are true for Qoheleth, and the tension is left standing (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: more gain (B); does more good (R)
decisions.reason: The book's wording for yitron (see 1:3), made comparative to fit the sentence.

records.source: הֶֽחָכָם֙ עֵינָ֣יו בְּרֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְהַכְּסִ֖יל בַּחֹ֣שֶׁךְ הוֹלֵ֑ךְ וְיָדַ֣עְתִּי גַם־אָ֔נִי שֶׁמִּקְרֶ֥ה אֶחָ֖ד יִקְרֶ֥ה אֶת־כֻּלָּֽם׃
records.gloss: The wise, his eyes [are] in his head, and the fool in darkness walks; and I knew, also I, that one fate will happen to all of them.
pieces: The wise have eyes in their heads, but the fool walks in the dark. Yet I also came to know that one fate comes to them all.

L.14: The wise—{{gender:their|his}} eyes [are] in {{gender:their|his}} head, but the fool walks in darkness; yet I also knew that one fate befalls them all.

R.14: Wise people can see where they are going, but a foolish person walks in the dark. But I also learned that the same thing happens to all of them in the end.

decisions.choice: eyes in his head: he sees where he is going
decisions.reason: A wise person sees the way ahead; the fool walks in the dark and stumbles (Proverbs 4:19).

decisions.choice: fool: a person set in folly
decisions.reason: The word (kesil) is the fool of Proverbs (1:22; 26:11): thick-headed, sure of himself, unwilling to learn. It returns often in this book (4:5; 5:3; 7:4-9; 10:2, 12).

decisions.choice: fate: what happens to a person, here death
decisions.reason: The word (miqreh) is what comes to someone, an event (Ruth 2:3), not blind chance. Here, as in 3:19 and 9:2-3, it is death, which comes to wise and fool alike.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: "The wise" stands for any wise person; the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: the fool (B); a foolish person (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for kesil, as in Proverbs: "fool" at Literal and Balanced, "foolish person" at Readable.

decisions.choice: can see where they are going
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom (m1).

records.source: וְאָמַ֨רְתִּֽי אֲנִ֜י בְּלִבִּ֗י כְּמִקְרֵ֤ה הַכְּסִיל֙ גַּם־אֲנִ֣י יִקְרֵ֔נִי וְלָ֧מָּה חָכַ֛מְתִּי אֲנִ֖י אָ֣ז יוֹתֵ֑ר וְדִבַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י שֶׁגַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: And I said, I, in my heart: As the fate of the fool, also it will happen to me, I; and why have I been wise, I, then, excessively? And I spoke in my heart that also this [is] breath.
pieces: Then I said to myself, "What happens to the fool will happen to me too. So why have I been so wise?" And I said to myself that this too is a breath.

L.15: And I said in my heart, "As [is] the fate of the fool, it will happen to me too; so why then have I been so very wise?" And I said in my heart that this too [is] breath.

R.15: I said to myself, "The same thing that happens to a foolish person will happen to me. So what good did it do me to be so wise?" I told myself that this too is like a breath, and I cannot make sense of it.

decisions.choice: so very: too much, to such advantage
alternatives: what extra have I gained by being wise
decisions.reason: The word (yoter) comes from the same root as "gain" (yitron). It can mean "very much" or "to what advantage": why has he been so wise, or what has wisdom gained him? Either way wisdom has bought him nothing against death.

decisions.choice: breath: beyond making sense of
decisions.reason: That the wise and the fool come to one end is something Qoheleth cannot make sense of; here hevel leans toward what cannot be grasped (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: like a breath, and I cannot make sense of it
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and says which sense of hevel is in view here (m2).

decisions.choice: I said to myself
decisions.reason: As in 1:16, Balanced and Readable use the English idiom.

records.source: כִּי֩ אֵ֨ין זִכְר֧וֹן לֶחָכָ֛ם עִֽם־הַכְּסִ֖יל לְעוֹלָ֑ם בְּשֶׁכְּבָ֞ר הַיָּמִ֤ים הַבָּאִים֙ הַכֹּ֣ל נִשְׁכָּ֔ח וְאֵ֛יךְ יָמ֥וּת הֶחָכָ֖ם עִֽם־הַכְּסִֽיל׃
records.gloss: For there is no remembrance of the wise with the fool forever, in that already the days coming, the all is forgotten; and how will die the wise with the fool!
pieces: For the wise will not be remembered forever, any more than the fool, since in the days to come all will be long forgotten. See how the wise die, just like fools!

L.16: For there is no remembrance of the wise with the fool forever, since in the days to come all will already have been forgotten. And how the wise dies just like the fool!

R.16: No one will remember the wise person forever, any more than the foolish person. In the days to come everyone will be forgotten. Wise people die just like foolish people do!

decisions.choice: how the wise dies: a cry of dismay
alternatives: How can the wise die like the fool? (a question)
decisions.reason: The word "how" ('ekh) often opens a lament (2 Samuel 1:19; Lamentations 1:1). Qoheleth cries out at what he has seen rather than asking for an answer.

decisions.choice: no remembrance: as in 1:11
decisions.reason: The poem of chapter 1 said the generations are forgotten (1:11); here even the wise share that end. Wisdom does not even leave a lasting name.

decisions.choice: will not be remembered (B); No one will remember (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:11, Balanced and Readable turn the noun into a verb.

records.source: וְשָׂנֵ֨אתִי֙ אֶת־הַ֣חַיִּ֔ים כִּ֣י רַ֤ע עָלַי֙ הַֽמַּעֲשֶׂ֔ה שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂ֖ה תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ כִּֽי־הַכֹּ֥ל הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: And I hated life, for evil upon me [was] the work which was done under the sun; for the all [is] breath and a chasing of wind.
pieces: So I hated life, because what is done under the sun weighed on me; everything is a breath and chasing the wind.

L.17: So I hated life, for the work that is done under the sun [was] evil to me, for everything [is] breath and a chasing of wind.

R.17: So I hated life. Everything that is done here on earth made me unhappy. All of it is like a breath. It is like trying to catch the wind.

decisions.choice: evil to me: grievous to me
decisions.reason: The word (ra') here means grievous or burdensome; it lay heavy on him (compare 6:1).

decisions.choice: the work that is done: all that happens in human life
decisions.reason: As in 1:14, "the work that is done under the sun" is everything people do and all that befalls them.

decisions.choice: weighed on me (B); made me unhappy (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense (m1); "evil" in modern English would suggest wickedness.

decisions.choice: a breath and chasing the wind (B); like a breath ... like trying to catch the wind (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording (see 1:2 and 1:14).

records.source: וְשָׂנֵ֤אתִֽי אֲנִי֙ אֶת־כָּל־עֲמָלִ֔י שֶׁאֲנִ֥י עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ שֶׁ֣אַנִּיחֶ֔נּוּ לָאָדָ֖ם שֶׁיִּהְיֶ֥ה אַחֲרָֽי׃
records.gloss: And I hated, I, all my toil which I [was] toiling under the sun, that I will leave it to the man who will be after me.
pieces: I hated all the hard work I had done under the sun, because I must leave what it earned to the one who comes after me.

L.18: And I hated all my toil at which I toiled under the sun, because I must leave it to the one who will come after me.

R.18: I hated all the hard work I had done here on earth. I would have to leave everything I had worked for to whoever comes after me.

decisions.choice: my toil: what my work earned
decisions.reason: Here 'amal is the wealth that toil produced, which can be left to someone else (see 1:3).

decisions.choice: the one who will come after me: an heir, whoever it may be
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) is a person in general, not a named heir. Qoheleth does not know who it will be (verse 19).

decisions.choice: what it earned (B); everything I had worked for (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that what is left is the fruit of the work (m1).

records.source: וּמִ֣י יוֹדֵ֗עַ הֶֽחָכָ֤ם יִהְיֶה֙ א֣וֹ סָכָ֔ל וְיִשְׁלַט֙ בְּכָל־עֲמָלִ֔י שֶֽׁעָמַ֥לְתִּי וְשֶׁחָכַ֖מְתִּי תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁ֑מֶשׁ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הָֽבֶל׃
records.gloss: And who knows whether a wise one he will be or a fool? And he will have power over all my toil which I toiled and which I was wise under the sun; also this [is] breath.
pieces: And who knows whether that one will be wise or a fool? Yet he will be master of all that I worked for and gained by wisdom under the sun. This too is a breath.

L.19: And who knows whether he will be wise or a fool? Yet he will rule over all my toil at which I toiled and at which I showed myself wise under the sun. This too [is] breath.

R.19: Who knows whether that person will be wise or foolish? But they will still control everything I worked so hard and so wisely for here on earth. This too is like a breath; I cannot hold on to it.

decisions.choice: fool: a senseless person
decisions.reason: This word (sakal) is not the usual word for a fool in this book (kesil, 2:14), but it means the same here (compare 10:3, 14).

decisions.choice: rule over: have full power to use or waste
decisions.reason: The verb (shalat) is to have mastery or control (5:18; 6:2; 8:9).

decisions.choice: breath: it slips out of one's hands
decisions.reason: What a person works for passes to someone else, who may waste it; here hevel leans toward what cannot be held on to (see the note at 1:2).

decisions.choice: a fool (B); foolish (R)
decisions.reason: The same wording as for kesil (2:14), since the sense is the same (m1).

decisions.choice: like a breath; I cannot hold on to it
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture and says which sense of hevel is in view (m3).

records.source: וְסַבּ֥וֹתִֽי אֲנִ֖י לְיַאֵ֣שׁ אֶת־לִבִּ֑י עַ֚ל כָּל־הֶ֣עָמָ֔ל שֶׁעָמַ֖לְתִּי תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: And I turned, I, to make my heart despair over all the toil which I toiled under the sun.
pieces: So I turned and gave my heart up to despair over all the hard work I had done under the sun.

L.20: So I turned to make my heart despair over all the toil at which I had toiled under the sun.

R.20: So I began to lose all hope about all the hard work I had done here on earth.

decisions.choice: I turned to make my heart despair: I gave myself up to despair
decisions.reason: The verb (ya'ash) means to give up hope (1 Samuel 27:1). "I turned" marks a change of course: from working to despairing of the work.

decisions.choice: lose all hope
decisions.reason: Readable uses everyday words for the idiom (m1).

records.source: כִּי־יֵ֣שׁ אָדָ֗ם שֶׁעֲמָל֛וֹ בְּחָכְמָ֥ה וּבְדַ֖עַת וּבְכִשְׁר֑וֹן וּלְאָדָ֞ם שֶׁלֹּ֤א עָֽמַל־בּוֹ֙ יִתְּנֶ֣נּוּ חֶלְק֔וֹ גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וְרָעָ֥ה רַבָּֽה׃
records.gloss: For there is a man whose toil [is] with wisdom and with knowledge and with skill, and to a man who did not toil in it he will give it [as] his portion; also this [is] breath and a great evil.
pieces: Someone may work with wisdom, knowledge and skill, and then must leave it all as the share of someone who never worked for it. This too is a breath and a great misfortune.

L.21: For there is a {{gender:person|man}} whose toil [is] with wisdom and with knowledge and with skill, and to a {{gender:person|man}} who has not toiled for it {{gender:they|he}} must give it [as] {{gender:that person's|his}} portion. This too [is] breath and a great evil.

R.21: A person may work hard and use wisdom, knowledge and skill. Then all they worked for goes to someone who did nothing for it, as what life gives to that other person. This too is like a breath, and it is a terrible thing.

decisions.choice: skill: competence that brings success
decisions.reason: The word (kishron) occurs only in this book (4:4; 5:10). It is ability that gets results.

decisions.choice: portion: here the share that passes to the heir
decisions.reason: The share (cheleq, see 2:10) that should have been the worker's own becomes the share of someone else.

decisions.choice: a great evil: a great misfortune, a wrong in the way things go
decisions.reason: The word (ra'ah) means evil in the sense of harm or misfortune as well as wrongdoing. Here no one sins; it is the way things fall out that is wrong (5:12, 15; 6:1).

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: a great misfortune (B); a terrible thing (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of ra'ah here (m3).

decisions.choice: share (B); what life gives (R)
decisions.reason: The book's settled wording for cheleq (see 2:10).

records.source: כִּ֠י מֶֽה־הֹוֶ֤ה לָֽאָדָם֙ בְּכָל־עֲמָל֔וֹ וּבְרַעְי֖וֹן לִבּ֑ושֶׁה֥וּא עָמֵ֖ל תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ׃
records.gloss: For what is coming to the man in all his toil and in the striving of his heart which he [is] toiling under the sun?
pieces: What do people get for all their hard work and all the striving of their hearts as they toil under the sun?

L.22: For what does a {{gender:person|man}} get from all {{gender:their|his}} toil and from the striving of {{gender:their|his}} heart at which {{gender:they toil|he toils}} under the sun?

R.22: People work hard and push themselves here on earth. But what do they get for all of it?

decisions.choice: the striving of his heart: the mind's anxious straining
decisions.reason: The word (ra'yon) is the one used in "a chasing of wind" (1:17; 4:16). With "heart" it is the inner effort and worry that go with the work.

decisions.choice: what does a person get: a question expecting "nothing that lasts"
decisions.reason: The verb (hovah, "to become, to come to") asks what comes of it all for the worker; verse 23 answers.

decisions.choice: inclusive wording by default; the traditional "he" or "man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses a masculine singular for a person who stands for anyone, so the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: people ... they
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word ('adam) means any human being. Balanced and Readable speak of people in general, which needs no setting; Literal keeps the singular with the gender setting.

decisions.choice: push themselves
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the inner striving (m1) in plain words.

records.source: כִּ֧י כָל־יָמָ֣יו מַכְאֹבִ֗ים וָכַ֨עַס֙ עִנְיָנ֔וֹ גַּם־בַּלַּ֖יְלָה לֹא־שָׁכַ֣ב לִבּ֑וֹ גַּם־זֶ֖ה הֶ֥בֶל הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: For all his days [are] pains, and vexation [is] his business; also at night his heart does not rest; also this [is] breath, it.
pieces: All their days are pain, and their work is vexation; even at night their minds do not rest. This too is a breath.

L.23: For all {{gender:their|his}} days [are] pains, and {{gender:their|his}} task [is] vexation; even at night {{gender:their|his}} heart does not rest. This too [is] breath.

R.23: All their days are full of pain, and their work makes them upset. Even at night their minds cannot rest. This too is like a breath.

decisions.choice: task: occupation, business (see 1:13)
decisions.reason: The word ('inyan) is the busy occupation God gave people (1:13). Here it brings vexation (ka'as, 1:18).

decisions.choice: at night his heart does not rest: worry keeps him awake
decisions.reason: The mind keeps working when the body lies down (compare 5:11).

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer back to the person of verse 22, who stands for anyone; the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default.

decisions.choice: like a breath
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture with "like" (see 1:2).

records.source: אֵֽין־ט֤וֹב בָּאָדָם֙ שֶׁיֹּאכַ֣ל וְשָׁתָ֔ה וְהֶרְאָ֧ה אֶת־נַפְשׁ֛וֹ ט֖וֹב בַּעֲמָל֑וֹ גַּם־זֹה֙ רָאִ֣יתִי אָ֔נִי כִּ֛י מִיַּ֥ד הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים הִֽיא׃
records.gloss: There is not good in the man that he will eat and drink and make his soul see good in his toil; also this I have seen, I, that from the hand of God it [is].
pieces: There is nothing better for people than to eat and drink and find enjoyment in their hard work. This too, I saw, comes from the hand of God.

L.24: There is nothing good for anyone [better] than that {{gender:they|he}} should eat and drink and let {{gender:their|his}} soul see good in {{gender:their|his}} toil. This also I saw: that from the hand of God it [is].

R.24: The best thing people can do is to eat and drink and enjoy their hard work. I saw that this also comes from God.

decisions.choice: there is nothing good ... than: nothing is better than
alternatives: it is not good for a person to eat and drink
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "there is no good in a person, that he eat". The same saying elsewhere in the book has "better than" or "except" (3:12, 22; 8:15), so the comparison is understood here. Some think a single letter meaning "than" was lost when the word before, which ends in the same letter, was copied.

decisions.choice: let his soul see good: enjoy, take pleasure
decisions.reason: "Soul" (nefesh) is the person himself, and "to see good" is to enjoy (2:1; 3:13).

decisions.choice: from the hand of God: enjoyment is God's gift, not a human achievement
decisions.reason: This is the first of the book's calls to enjoy food, drink and work (3:12-13, 22; 5:17-19; 8:15; 9:7-10; 11:9). They stand beside the cry that everything is breath (2:17), and the book leaves both standing (see the note at 1:2). What a person cannot gain by toil, God can give.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they|he}} ... {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer to anyone; the gender setting gives inclusive wording by default and the traditional form as the alternative.

decisions.choice: [better]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the comparison the Hebrew leaves understood (m1).

decisions.choice: comes from God
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense of the idiom.

records.source: כִּ֣י מִ֥י יֹאכַ֛ל וּמִ֥י יָח֖וּשׁ ח֥וּץ מִמֶּֽנִּי׃
records.gloss: For who will eat and who will enjoy outside of me?
pieces: For who can eat or who can find enjoyment apart from me?

L.25: For who can eat, and who can enjoy, apart from me?

R.25: After all, who has eaten and enjoyed life more than I have?

decisions.choice: apart from me: the Hebrew text
alternatives: apart from him: the reading of the ancient Greek and Syriac translations, which makes God the giver of enjoyment
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "apart from me": Qoheleth, who tried every pleasure (2:4-10), speaks from experience, and no one has tasted more than he. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read "apart from him", which ties the verse to verse 24: no one can eat or enjoy without God. The difference is one letter in Hebrew. The Hebrew text is followed. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: enjoy: take pleasure
decisions.reason: The verb (chush) usually means to hurry. Here many take it from a like-sounding root meaning to feel or enjoy, which fits "eat"; others read "worry".

decisions.choice: who has eaten and enjoyed life more than I have?
alternatives: who can eat and who can enjoy apart from me?
decisions.reason: Readable says what "apart from me" means in the reading followed (m1).

records.source: כִּ֤י לְאָדָם֙ שֶׁטּ֣וֹב לְפָנָ֔יו נָתַ֛ן חָכְמָ֥ה וְדַ֖עַת וְשִׂמְחָ֑ה וְלַחוֹטֶא֩ נָתַ֨ן עִנְיָ֜ן לֶאֱס֣וֹף וְלִכְנ֗וֹס לָתֵת֙ לְטוֹב֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הָֽאֱלֹהִ֔ים גַּם־זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ׃
records.gloss: For to a man who [is] good before him, he has given wisdom and knowledge and joy; and to the sinner he has given the business to gather and to collect, to give to [one] good before God. Also this [is] breath and a chasing of wind.
pieces: God gives wisdom, knowledge and joy to the one who pleases {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; but to the sinner {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives the task of gathering and storing up, only to hand it over to the one who pleases God. This too is a breath and chasing the wind.

L.26: For to the {{gender:person|man}} who [is] good before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given wisdom and knowledge and joy; but to the sinner {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given the task of gathering and collecting, to give to the one [who is] good before God. This too [is] breath and a chasing of wind.

R.26: God gives wisdom, knowledge and joy to people who please {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives sinners the job of gathering and storing up wealth, only to give it to people who please God. This too is like a breath. It is like trying to catch the wind.

decisions.choice: good before him: pleasing to God
decisions.reason: The phrase means one who pleases God, whom God favors (7:26). The sinner (chote') is one who misses the mark and so displeases him. The words can be heard of moral goodness, or of God's free favor; the book does not explain, but leaves the giving with God (verse 24).

decisions.choice: the sinner gathers for the one who pleases God
decisions.reason: Proverbs 13:22 says the same: the wealth of the sinner is stored up for the righteous (compare Job 27:16-17).

decisions.choice: this too is breath: the sinner's gathering, or the whole arrangement
decisions.reason: The refrain may refer to the sinner's toil, which comes to nothing for him, or to the whole of what verses 24-26 describe, which no one can make sense of or control. Either way Qoheleth ends the chapter with his refrain.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}
decisions.reason: Pronouns for God take the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: God gives ... to the one who pleases him
alternatives: To the one who is good before him he gives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God at the start, so that the pronouns have something to refer to.

decisions.choice: wealth
decisions.reason: Readable names what the sinner gathers, which the Hebrew leaves understood.
